subject: Request: Incident notification scope & evidence access under DPA
messages:
From: Claire Hsu <security@finbridge.co>
To: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@brightbank.com
Date: 2027-03-30T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Potential data exposure affecting FinBridge - initial notification

Hi Ben,

FinBridge detected anomalous access patterns in a subset of inference request logs that may include customer identifiers. We are still triaging but wanted to notify Redwood immediately per the DPA (section 5). Can you confirm: 

- Your expected notification timeline under the DPA for incidents involving customer identifiers;
- Whether Redwood can provide an evidence snapshot and audit logs to our security team (and how that transfer would work);
- If subprocessors would be engaged and whether any international transfers are required.

We are preparing a request for forensic access and would prefer a documented plan for evidence preservation and transfer. Please let us know the right contact and an initial timeline.

Thanks,
Claire Hsu
Head of Security, FinBridge
security@finbridge.co

(Attachment: finbridge-incident-summary.txt)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Hsu <security@finbridge.co>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-03-30T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure affecting FinBridge - initial notification

Claire — thanks for the heads up and sorry to hear you're seeing anomalous activity. We take these requests seriously and will treat this as a DPA-triggered notification.

Quick acknowledgement and proposed immediate steps: 
1) Acknowledged — Redwood will confirm a formal notice within 72 hours per our DPA section on incident notifications.
2) Evidence preservation — we will take a forensic snapshot of the affected logs and preserve all relevant KV cache and telemetry. Our infra lead (Marissa) will coordinate the snapshot.
3) Evidence transfer — we can provide an encrypted, auditable transfer (signed S3 URL with access logs) or set up a secure-access bucket for FinBridge security.
4) Subprocessors — we'll confirm whether any of our data handling partners (e.g., CloudTransferCo, RedisEdge) are implicated; if so, we'll include the subprocessors list and any transfer agreements.

Looping in: Kimberly (legal) to confirm DPA timings and any redlines; Marissa (infra) for export; Laura (procurement/CS) for SLA/contract questions.

Internal team — can you confirm: 1) feasible forensic snapshot timing (ETA), 2) whether export will include encrypted transfer plus audit logs, and 3) whether subprocessors need to be notified?

Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-03-30T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure affecting FinBridge - initial notification

Ben / team — quick internal breakout:

- Legal: I will own DPA interpretation and confirm the 72-hour window applicability. Per our standard DPA, we have an obligation to notify customers without undue delay and cooperate with reasonable forensic access requests; I'll attach a short excerpt (dpa-extract-notify-clause.txt).
- Infra (Marissa): can you commit to a forensic snapshot within 24 hours and provide an integrity-hashed export (SHA256) plus audit logs showing retrievals? We should produce a minimal evidence slice (timestamps, request ids, truncated payloads) rather than wholesale full logs.
- Procurement/CS (Laura): please prep a statement on whether we need to offer escrow/third-party forensics or contract accommodations; also confirm whether procurement@brightbank.com should be looped for contractual triggers.

Subprocessors: initial check of our subproc roster indicates CloudTransferCo (log transport) and RedisEdge (KV caching) are the only likely touchpoints. If either is implicated, we'll need to follow the subprocessor notification process in our DPA and provide their contact info.

Attachments: redwood-incident-runbook-v2.pdf (runbook excerpt), dpa-extract-notify-clause.txt (legal excerpt).

Marissa, can you confirm timelines and whether export requires any cross-border transfer that would trigger additional consent?

-Kim
Kimberly Park | Counsel, Privacy & Security
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
(Attachment: dpa-extract-notify-clause.txt)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Hsu <security@finbridge.co>
Cc: procurement@brightbank.com, kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-03-30T16:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure affecting FinBridge - initial notification

Claire — following internal validation, here's the initial cooperation plan we can commit to: 

1) Notification window: Redwood confirms a formal incident notice within 72 hours of this message in line with our DPA notification clause. Kimberly will attach the excerpt for your records.

2) Forensic snapshot & preservation: Marissa will produce a integrity-checked forensic snapshot of the affected logs within 48 hours (we initially scoped 24 hours but want to be conservative to ensure completeness). The export will include SHA256 checksums, time-bounded slices (start/end timestamps), request IDs, and redacted payloads where necessary.

3) Evidence transfer method: We will provide a signed, time-limited S3 URL with server-side encryption + CloudTrail access logs for auditing. If you prefer direct secure transfer to an SFTP endpoint you provide, we can accommodate that.

4) Subprocessors & transfers: Current check shows potential involvement from CloudTransferCo and RedisEdge. If either is implicated, we'll follow DPA subprocessor notification and provide contact details and any relevant subprocessor agreements. No cross-border transfer is expected at this time; Marissa will confirm.

5) Next steps: proposed forensics kickoff call tomorrow at 10:00 AM PT to align on scope and required artifacts. If that works, we'll send a calendar invite.

Attachments: redwood-incident-runbook-v2.pdf (runbook excerpt), dpa-extract-notify-clause.txt (DPA excerpt).

Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0123
